reviews.title: Great Product
reviews.comment: The AsiaHorse COSMIQ 120mm case fan delivers a solid mix of performance and aesthetics, especially if you’re building or upgrading a PC on a budget but still want a clean-looking setup. The RGB lighting is surprisingly vibrant and adds a nice visual touch through a tempered glass case without looking overly flashy or cheap. In terms of cooling, the fan does a respectable job improving airflow, especially when used as part of a multi-fan setup. It keeps internal temperatures stable during gaming and general workloads, and noise levels stay fairly controlled at normal speeds. It’s not the quietest premium fan on the market, but it strikes a reasonable balance between airflow and sound. Installation is straightforward, and the build quality feels decent for the price point. The frame is sturdy enough, and the cables are manageable, though not as refined as higher-end brands. Syncing the RGB with common motherboard software worked without much hassle in my case. Overall, this is a good value option if you want decent cooling performance with attractive lighting without spending premium-tier money. It’s best suited for budget-to-midrange builds where aesthetics still matter but cost efficiency is a priority.
reviews.author: Johnnyb

reviews.title: Pretty awesome
reviews.comment: I added the AsiaHorse COSMIQ 120mm fans to my PC build, and they made a huge difference right away. The airflow is strong and consistent, which helped lower my case temperatures compared to the older fans I had. Even when the system is running heavier tasks, the fans stay smooth without extra noise. The RGB lighting is bright and clean-looking, with colors that blend well and don’t flicker. They give the case a really polished look without being overly flashy. The build quality also feels solid, and the fans don’t vibrate or rattle once installed. Installation was simple, and all the mounting hardware fit exactly as it should. The cables are tidy and easy to manage, which helps keep the inside of the case organized. If you want fans that look good and keep your system cool without sounding loud or cheap, these are a great choice. They add both style and performance to a setup, and it was easy to connect.
reviews.author: Viral Fixes Daily

reviews.title: Love Them
reviews.comment: The daisy chain on these is amazing. I know multiple companies are have started doing this type of snap together daisy chain now but this is my first time having fans like this and it makes the installation so much easier. I love the look of them, they’re extremely clean. Also these fans are very quiet and work very well. My temps are great, I really only game on my pc and even at high settings, gpu might hit 60-65°c under a heavier load(4070ti) and cpu is roughly the same (Ryzen 7 7800x3d). Overall I really think these fans are definitely worth the money for performance and aesthetic
reviews.author: Kristy S

reviews.title: Pretty nice, brand name in the mirror is kinda weird??
reviews.comment: ETA: Changed from four to five stars! Customer service was exceptional. I reached out to see if there was some way I could get a set without the brand name. Apparently they have phased those out (because they know people prefer the cleaner look) and they immediately sent me a matching set. Love seeing support like that! Will definitely be keeping up with this company. I do really like these fans overall. I actually got some reverse fans as a gift from a friend and decided to upgrade my other AsiaHorse fans to this one so they match-matched. Unfortunately, they seem to branding in the side mirrors now? Or they stopped and I got older ones? I'm not sure. But either way they uh...don't match-match! Part of my big draw to these was that they looked great and weren't heavily branded like so many PC products are. That's the reason I'm pointing it out. The mirrors are cool, but I don't really want to see the same name glowing over and over in my case lol. So if that's something that bothers you too, it's definitely a skip. Overall. I do like them. They can get loud, but if you can run at a lower fan curve that shouldn't be an issue. But if you have one of those mics that just refuses to mute out any sound around you, your friends may hear them when you're at higher speeds due to load. The bumper pads definitely help with noise, but it may take some adjusting to remove all buzzing from vibration, depending on your case. I did message asking if there was anyway to get ones without the name, because I'm the kind of person that it'll bother me. But if that's not possible, I'll probably be downgrading back to their similar but cheaper fans.
reviews.author: Dancing Coin

reviews.title: Budget friendly, high quality, while maintaining a sleek Rgb look
reviews.comment: Beautiful looking fans while still maintaining good airflow and quietness. Super easy to cable manage with 1 cable for 3 fans. Colors, no problem, they have plenty of leds inside the fan itself for endless customization. My motherboard software had no issues doing any customization or fan control. Only complaint is i got 1 fan that’s off balanced or something inside is misaligned, at 80% power or above i can feel it humming and vibrating. Other than that one small issue they’re great, they look good, and they’re way cheaper than anything else of this variety.
